title: Republicans zero in on key player accused of helping Democrat fundraising giant hide foreign cash
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Republicans zero in on key player accused of helping Democrat fundraising giant hide foreign cash

House Republicans summon ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview, citing contradictions in his prior statements on donor verification.

Rep. James Comer, R-KY, joins Fox Across America with guest host Paul Mauro to provide an update on the House Oversight Committee's investigation on alleged fraud by fundraising platform ActBlue.

FIRST ON FOX: House Republicans' investigation into Democrats' main fundraising platform is heating up on the heels of an explosive report that raised questions about whether left-wing candidates' campaigns were raking in foreign cash.

Top House GOP committee chairs are summoning ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview sometime before Oct. 9, Fox News Digital has learned. A letter sent to Machen Monday morning stated that information he previously disclosed to investigators appears to contradict other data that has been collected, specifically on ActBlue's verification standards for making sure a donor is a U.S. citizen.

"On September 11, 2026, you provided a briefing to the House Administration, Judiciary, and Oversight and Government Reform Committees regarding the accuracy of ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones’s prior statements to Congress about ActBlue’s donor and passport collection processes," the letter said.

"Your review appears to be nothing more than an after-the-fact sugarcoating of ActBlue’s misconduct and Ms. Wallace-Jones’s misrepresentations to the House Administration Committee."

ANOTHER ACTBLUE LEADER PLEADS FIFTH AS HOUSE INVESTIGATES ALLEGED FOREIGN DONATIONS

ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones prepares to testify before the House Administration Committee's hearing on "Preventing Fraudulent Donations: Transparency, Verification, and Accountability" in Washington, D.C., on June 10, 2026. Wallace-Jones invoked the Fifth Amendment during questioning. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

The letter was sent by House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., and House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., who lead the panels probing ActBlue.

ACTBLUE CO-FOUNDER PLEADS FIFTH AMENDMENT IN CLOSED-DOOR HOUSE GOP GRILLING

ActBlue is a massive platform for campaigns to raise money that's used by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and the Democratic leaders of the House and Senate, among others.

Republican lawmakers have long accused the company of having lax verification standards for donors, something ActBlue has said it actively improved since the start of the GOP's probe. But a new report released earlier this month, first reported by Fox News Digital, appears to show employees green-lighting donations despite some questions about where they came from.

FAR-LEFT POLITICIANS STILL USING ACTBLUE AS 88-YEAR-OLD DISPUTES DONATING NEARLY $150,000 TO FUNDRAISING GIANT

Chief among the GOP's concerns is ActBlue's passport number verification. According to the report, the field only requires the correct number of characters for a U.S. passport number rather than a valid code for a donation to be accepted.

The Monday letter also points to a 2024 "contemporaneous review by ActBlue’s then-outside counsel, former Biden White House Counsel Dana Remus" which allegedly found "'a substantial risk that some of the funds' raised for Democrat campaigns and causes by ActBlue 'were impermissible contributions from foreign nationals.'"

Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, and House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer are investigating ActBlue. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images; Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images; Finn Gomez/Getty Images)
